newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy appeals to parties as Albania faces crisis.
newsitem.headline: Italy appeals to parties as Albania faces crisis.

text.p: Italy appealed to Albania's political parties on Tuesday to avoid a dangerous slide into a new crisis and said the next 24 hours could be crucial.

"The next 24 hours are very important for the future of Albania," Defence Minister Beniamino Andreatta told reporters after addressing a parliamentary commission on the multinational security force that Italy is leading in Albania.

He spoke after Albanian Prime Minister Bashkim Fino appealed for Western help and warned that political deadlock over elections due next month had pushed the country to the brink of a "deeper crisis with unforseen consequences".

Prime Minister Romano Prodi, on a visit to Budapest, said Italy would work to the "last hours" to convince Albanian parties to hold elections. If that failed, he said the security mission would have to be revised.

Andreatta called on all sides "to overcome arrogance and diffidence and to seek together, notwithstanding the splits that have occurred, to legitimise the electoral process with reciprocal concessions".

Albanian President Sali Berisha has called elections in the volatile Balkan state for June 29, but most parties have threatened to boycott the vote because they say current election laws favour Berisha's rightist Democratic Party.
Marathon talks between parties have so far failed to resolve the deadlock. Fino leads a Government of National Reconciliation, installed at the height of unrest.

Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini warned that Albania could slide back into the chaos of February and March when the collapse of crooked investment schemes, in which thousands lost their life savings, unleashed violence and looting.

"The primary objective at the moment is to halt a dangerous trend that could set Albania back weeks and compromise the whole delicate process of reconciliation that has been carried out so far," Dini told a parliamentary hearing.
Italian news agencies quoted Prime Minister Romano Prodi as saying international mediator Franz Vranitzky had urged the parties to talk until midnight to try to unblock the situation.

Vranitzky, an envoy of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe, has repeatedly travelled to Tirana to try to broker a deal on elections. There was no immediate confirmation of the reports.
Andreatta said the coming days were "crucial" and the international community must do all it could to facilitate a deal.

He said the United Nations Security Council would also have to examine a possible extension of its three-month mandate for the security force, which has been overseeing aid deliveries in the chaotic state.
The force's mandate runs out one day before the planned vote, on June 28.

Andreatta has in the past suggested that the mandate, which does not allow troops to disarm Albanians who seized guns from state armouries when law and order collapsed, should be widened to help oversee the elections.
